props.lens:
RIGOR/ROBUSTNESS. Goal: make the existing positive results (B2 73/110, H2 88/110, B3 22 vs 8, LB 127/180) trustworthy and publishable through replication, causal isolation, statistics, contamination checks, compute accounting, independent re-scoring and CPU-only forensics on outputs that already exist. Grounding: I ran unregistered, read-only scratch checks on the logged F caches and plan files (scripts in C:/Users/clclc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bwm_next_scratch/: freplay.py, forest.py, legality.py, unparsed.py, anytime.py, wellplaced.py, clusters.py). They are pure Python plus bwmn/blocks.py, with no torch. Four findings change the plan:
(1) The learned F made almost no errors that affected a plan. In B2-hard, 6 of 20,530 queried keys were false-illegal, and H2-hard had 5 of 22,895. All of them are in hard/instance-102, which both runs solved. There were 0 false-legal answers that the planner accepted and 0 wrong next states. So the exact-F ceiling on hard equals the observed 73 and 88.
(2) F's own `legal` flag is wrong on many of the illegal actions the proposer actually emits. It says "legal" on 798/4,066 (19.6%) in B2-hard and 657/2,363 (27.8%) in H2-hard; mostly these are pick-up of a block that sits on another block. Every one was rejected only by parse_forward_delta's support check (a predicted deletion of a fact the state lacks gives None). Rates are similar in the mirror (24%), PB-600 (13%) and B3 distillation (22%). So 'every verified plan valid' and B3's label precision 1.000 rely on that code check.
(3) H2's gain is mostly dead-end repair. Of the 20 instances that only Pa_v3 solved, 14 were B2 dead_ends and 6 were budget failures. B2 dead-ends stopped with budget unused (mean 8.5k vs 15.0k tokens). The illegal share of F queries fell from 19.8% to 10.3%. Of the failed runs, 28/37 (B2) and 19/22 (H2) reached an imagined state with exactly 1 unmet goal fact that still had 1-12 misplaced blocks. These are deceptive minima of the unmet key.
(4) The anytime curve is exact under a round cap, because CRN seeds and the memoised F make the beam independent of the cap. H2 is at or above B2 at every proposer-token budget of 6k or more (8k: 61 vs 53; 12k: 80 vs 65).
Hard goal shapes are barely clustered (87 distinct (n, goal tower shape) classes in 110), so instance-level CIs are adequate. Item 7 is in flight (BW_Fdelta_s1 at step 350/600, no FREEZE_I7_* yet), so addenda can still be written before its freeze.

proposals.title: Test-time world-model fidelity and legality-attribution audit (registered CPU replay of every logged F query)
proposals.question: On the transitions the frozen planners actually queried, how often is F wrong (false-illegal, false-legal, wrong state)? Which of these errors reached a beam decision? How much of the 'every verified plan valid' property (P-08/P-10/P-14) and of B3's label precision 1.000 (P-11) depends on parse_forward_delta's support check rather than on F's learned legality?
proposals.why_now: The H2 headline is about to go into the README, model card and GitHub export (D-49, D-65, H2_LEAK_CLAIMS_AUDIT.json headline). The scratch replay shows a scope problem nobody has recorded. F-07 says 'several' delta legality errors are caught by the parser. The real rate is 19.6-27.8% of the illegal actions queried at test time, and blocks_planner.plan_beam's docstring says 'the domain rules are known only to the learned F'. The audit also decides, before the B4 draft (research/PREREG_B4_DRAFT.md §8.5) and the Logistics draft freeze, whether an exact-F oracle arm is worth any GPU. It must also be registered before FREEZE_I7_* so the item-7 replicates get the same metric.
proposals.expected_value:
High, at zero GPU cost.
- It turns the strongest claim ('verified plans are always valid') from an observation into a mechanism with the right scope, before anything goes public. That avoids a later retraction of the wording.
- It settles that the learned world model is not the bottleneck on hard: about 0 of the 37 B2 and 22 H2 failures come from F. This saves the oracle-ceiling GPU arm in B4 (an estimated 1-2 turns).
- It names the next F repair target with a test-time metric: about 20-28% false-legal on pick-up of a stacked block. This is the same failure class as F-01, P-12, X-01 and X-04, and it gives the FK+trace candidate in P-12 a concrete success criterion.
proposals.risks: Forest reconstruction keys states by content. In shards where two instances share a block alphabet, an identical state could mix forests; this is harmless for the error counts, so it is noted as a limitation. If the registered replay disagrees with the scratch numbers, the registered one stands. The finding qualifies existing wording, and the user may see that as a downgrade. It is not, because the check is domain-agnostic and is also used in the Logistics draft, but it must be disclosed. The audit does not show what would happen without the check; that needs proposal 7.

proposals.title: Failure forensics, exact anytime curves and a per-instance compute ledger for B2 vs H2 (CPU)
proposals.question: Why do the 37 B2 and 22 H2 hard failures fail: proposer collapse (illegal or repeated candidates, a tiny forest), beam death with budget left (dead_end), or deceptive minima of the unmet-goal ranking key? Does H2's advantage hold at every matched compute budget, not only at the frozen cap?
proposals.why_now:
Two things depend on this.
- B4 (critic) and B5 (macros) are the next joint GPU items. Their power and arm choice depend on how many failures are ranking-limited vs proposer-limited.
- P-14 says 'the gain does not come from more search' from two means only (8.2k vs 8.0k tokens). The scratch cross-tab shows 14 of H2's 20 wins were B2 dead_ends, and the B4 draft's c+pen control may be identical to c with this F.
proposals.expected_value:
High.
- It gives H2 a mechanism: the distilled proposer emits half as many illegal actions (10.3% vs 19.8% of F queries) and avoids beam death.
- It replaces a two-number compute argument with a dominance curve.
- It gives B4 an evidence-based power estimate. Scratch: 28/37 B2 failures sit at deceptive unmet=1 minima, so a better critic has room.
- It may save one 110-instance B4 arm, about 2 GPU turns, through the c ≡ c+pen certificate.
- It produces the FLOPs accounting that E-01(c) records as not run.
proposals.risks: The h* computation at 12-15 blocks may not finish for some states; report those as missing, never drop them. Token-budget curves are approximate between rounds; only the round-cap curve is exact. Forensic categories are descriptive and must not be used to select any B4/B5 setting on hard; selection stays on generated sets. Do not run anything new on hard.

proposals.title: Vendored, VAL-scored per-instance pairing against published LRMs, with a per-instance token and FLOP ledger (post hoc, labelled)
proposals.question: On the same 110 Blocksworld-hard instances, how do B2 and H2 compare per instance with DeepSeek-R1, o1-preview and o1-mini direct (step-0) attempts? At what inference compute?
proposals.why_now: The user's goal is to show whether small Rineya world models rival larger models. P-14 correction (d) found that 'aggregate only' was false: per-instance upstream files exist at fc638a1a. It forbids citing paired results until those files are vendored with sha256 and re-scored with the local VAL. The audit's simulator-only numbers (H2 vs R1 +36/−7, p = 9e-6; B2 vs R1 +30/−16, p = 0.054) are uncitable until then. The upstream files also carry per-instance token usage: R1 mean 7,797 completion tokens, o1-preview 7,732, o1-mini 12,188, with reasoning tokens split out. That makes an honest compute comparison possible now.
proposals.expected_value: High for the user's headline question. It replaces an unpaired Fisher test with a VAL-verified paired comparison on identical instances. It adds the first quantitative compute contrast: a 0.6B core with about 8.2k proposer tokens plus about 200 F queries, against about 7.8k reasoning-heavy tokens on a 37B-active model. My rough expectation, to be computed, is about an order of magnitude fewer inference FLOPs per instance for BWM before amortized training. The complementarity list shows where the LRMs still win.
proposals.risks: Vendoring is a write into bench/ and needs the user's approval. Extraction ambiguity could move a few instances, hence two extractors. Reviewers may still see a domain-trained specialist with search vs zero-shot generalists as apples to oranges. The regime caveat and the input-format difference (parsed JSON vs PDDL text) must lead every table. o1 parameter counts are unknown, so only tokens can be compared there.

proposals.title: Causal isolation and fresh-set replication of H2, folded into B4's fresh set (adds a Pa_v2c × default-hook arm)
proposals.question: Is H2's +15 caused by the content of the self-distilled plans, or by 400 extra training steps? Does the Pa_v3 vs Pa_v2 beam gain replicate on fresh hard-style instances, and is the hard-vs-fresh gap for the Pa_v3 beam within the 10 pp contamination flag?
proposals.why_now: P-14 states that the registered contrast 'does not separate the search-plan content from the extra training. There is no Pa_v2c beam arm on hard'. The only support is the S-direct control (P-11: v2c vs v2 +6/−3). H2 has no mirror or fresh-set run either, so there is no contamination flag for the headline. The D-70 follow-up already plans c and a under Pa_v3 as B4 secondaries on the fresh seed-20261410 set, which is not generated yet (X-06). Adding one arm now costs one bundle slot and no extra hard exposure.
proposals.design:
Amend the B4 draft (research/PREREG_B4_DRAFT.md) before its freeze. Fresh set: seed 20261410, n = 110, hard block mix, generated with the B4 freeze after item 7, excluding everything in D-70/X-06 plus seeds_fresh. All arms use the frozen B2 beam args (runs/FREEZE_B2_beam.json, K8 W4 E24 R12 M80 P1, delta F BW_Fdelta_s0, planner 18a5f22b…) with the default unmet hook.
Arms:
- c×Pa_v2: the B4 control, already planned;
- c×Pa_v3: already planned as a secondary;
- NEW c×Pa_v2c (runs/BW_Pa_v2c_s1, sha f7ac53bf…, frozen in FREEZE_B3 before any hard run).
Registered secondary family, Holm m = 2, exact McNemar:
- S1, H2 replication: c×Pa_v3 vs c×Pa_v2. Reading REPLICATES iff v3-only > v2-only and Holm p < 0.05.
- S2, isolation: c×Pa_v3 vs c×Pa_v2c. Reading 'gain attributable to distilled plans' iff v3-only > v2c-only and Holm p < 0.05.
Report-only:
- c×Pa_v2c vs c×Pa_v2 (the extra-training effect in the beam);
- the hard-minus-fresh gap for the Pa_v3 beam (88/110 vs the fresh rate), with the P-10 goal-tower-bin reweighting now pre-registered;
- the proposal-2 forensics on all arms.
Power: if hard's discordance holds (23%, 4:1), n = 110 gives roughly 0.85 for S1.
Fallback if B4 slips: 'H3' = c×Pa_v2c on hard-110, run once (one new hard exposure, logged in proposal 6's exposure ledger), paired with the existing H2 run.
proposals.expected_value: This is the decisive answer to the most obvious reviewer objection to the headline: was it just more training? It also gives a second, fresh-set replication of the 73 to 88 gain and closes the missing contamination flag for H2. If proposal 2's c ≡ c+pen certificate holds, the extra arm costs nothing net against the current B4 plan.
proposals.risks: Each 110-instance beam arm takes about 8 GPU-h (D-50), and the queue is about 2-3 BWM turns a day. B4's freeze waits on item 7, so the answer is days away. If Pa_v2c ≈ Pa_v3 on the fresh set, H2's wording must change to 'more proposer training in the beam', which is an honest but weaker claim. The fresh set's goal structure is not matched to hard (the P-09/P-10 lesson), so the gap must be read with the reweighting.

proposals.title: Seed replication of the distillation step (B3/Pa_v3), as an item-7 addendum written before FREEZE_I7_*
proposals.question: Is B3's 'met' reading (Pa_v3 22/110 vs Pa_v2c 8/110 S-direct, P-11), and so the proposer behind H2, robust to the training seed? Optionally: does the whole expert-iteration step reproduce inside an independently seeded system?
proposals.why_now: PREREG_ITEM7_SEEDS.md replicates only B2 (F and Pa_v2 seeds). Its 'Not claimed' section explicitly excludes seed robustness of Pa_v3, yet the current headline (P-14) rests on one Pa_v3 seed. Item 7 is still training F seed 1 (runs/BW_Fdelta_s1 at step 350/600; no FREEZE_I7_* written), so an addendum can be registered now without touching the frozen item-7 tests.
proposals.expected_value: It removes the 'one training seed' caveat from the headline's key component at modest cost. Trainings take about 7,600 s and 6,600 s per pair (D-63 estimates), and S-direct evaluation takes minutes. A failure to replicate would be important to learn before any public release (the D-65 release gate). The full-pipeline variant would turn 'self-distillation worked once' into 'expert iteration with a learned world model replicates in an independent system'.
proposals.risks: It competes with B4/B5/item 9 for turns. The training-seed version holds the distillation rows fixed, so it does not test variance in the search data; only the stretch does. S-direct effects are small (8-22 per 110), so one pair can miss the +10 pp bar by noise; the registered both-pairs rule can then read 'not replicated' for a real but noisy effect. State that power limit in the prereg.

proposals.title: Claims ledger, hard-set exposure budget and errata carry-through (release-gate hygiene)
proposals.question: Is every public-facing number traceable to a registered test or labelled post hoc, with the right multiplicity family and the required caveats? How many more times may the reserved hard-110 be used?
proposals.why_now:
Several records are inconsistent and must be fixed before release, vault or HF, and before the user's full GitHub backup:
- The H2 audit found the o1-mini '10% zero-shot' row (really LRM-Modulo) in release README:40, SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md:44 and PREREG_PLANBENCH.md:117 (hash-frozen, so it needs an erratum).
- It also found 'aggregate only' (README:42), 'trained only on…' (gh-export README:59), goal on-pairs '5-12' (really 4-13) and FR-01 rounding.
- Proposal 1 adds a new scope item (the support check).
- Hard-110 has already been used by four frozen configurations (B2 beam, B2 direct, H1, H2) with no stated cap.
proposals.expected_value: Medium. It is cheap, it is required for any credible release, and it stops the over-claims the audit found from spreading into the card. The exposure budget protects the hard set's value as a test instrument for B4/B5. The ledger doubles as a checklist for the user's commit-and-backup request.
proposals.risks: Purely documentary, so it is easy to postpone; it should be done before the next export rather than after. Edits to hash-frozen files are forbidden; use erratum files only. Agreeing a cap on hard exposures may need the user's sign-off, because it constrains later GPU plans (proposal 4's fallback, B4/B5 on hard).

proposals.title: Support-check ablation: how much does the delta-consistency check contribute to planning success and verification precision? (report-only, generated set)
proposals.question: If the planner trusted F's own `legal` flag (applying the predicted adds and only the deletions that actually hold), how many 'verified' plans would be invalid, and how would success change? This measures what the learned F knows about legality without the code-side check.
proposals.why_now: This follows from proposal 1's finding (19.6-27.8% of proposer-emitted illegal actions are claimed legal by F and rescued only by the parser). Before the Logistics prereg freezes (it reuses parse_forward_delta) and before any 'learned world model' wording is finalized, the size of the check's contribution should be measured directly, not inferred.
proposals.expected_value: Medium. It gives a precise sentence for the card, of the form: 'without the consistency check, verification precision falls from 1.00 to X on generated hard-style problems.' It either confirms that the learned legality head is the weak link or shows the check rarely matters for success. It also motivates (or deprioritizes) the FK+trace legality repair listed as P-12's next candidate.
proposals.risks: Thirty instances give a coarse estimate, so it is descriptive only. The trusting parser is one of several possible no-check variants; pre-specify it exactly. It uses part of a turn that B4/B5/item 9 could use, so it may be better appended to an existing bundle's leftover time (the D-41 fit-or-skip rule) than given its own turn.

props.lens: CAPABILITY: planning intelligence gained per shared-GPU turn. Three read-only CPU checks (scratch scripts in C:/Users/clclc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bwm_next_scratch/) drive the ranking. (1) I replayed all 48,388 unique F queries in the generated-set planning caches against B.step: mirror S-beam 23,752, distill-240 15,030, BW_SELECT_v1 9,606. There is exactly one planning-relevant F error, a false 'illegal' at 15 blocks. No illegal action is accepted. All 1,881 unparseable answers fall on illegal actions, so rollout_many stops correctly. Between 11% and 19% of the queries are illegal proposals from Pa. F is therefore not the bottleneck at 15 blocks or fewer; the proposer and search are. (2) I rebuilt the 2,400 P-12 prompts (0 sha mismatches) and re-scored them the way the planner reads them. FK's effective accuracy is canon 1.000, heldout_rev 0.996, heldout_other 0.996, heldout_both 0.942, with 0 illegal actions accepted. The reason: in blocksworld-4ops every precondition is in its action's delete list, so parse_forward_delta's support check rejects a wrong 'legal' answer. P-12's legality cost is therefore not planning-relevant in Blocksworld. This does NOT carry over to Logistics, whose domain file never deletes at ?truck ?loc, at ?airplane ?loc, in-city, AIRPORT or the type facts. (3) Along the mirror beam plans at 11-15 blocks, unmet goal facts stay flat for a mean longest run of 9.5-10.1 steps, against R=12. This plateau length does not separate successes from failures, so it motivates B4 but does not prove it. Mirror B2 failures are 44/74 at 11-15 blocks vs 5/36 at 6-10 (27 budget, 22 dead end). These are post-hoc and report-only. All analyses use generated sets only, never hard.

proposals.title: B6: second round of search distillation (Pa_v4) on 11-15-block problems, with a matched control and a 512-token direct cap
proposals.question: Can a second expert-iteration round lift the proposer, and then the system, past Pa_v3 where Pa_v3 still fails? The teacher is the H2 system (Pa_v3 + BW_Fdelta_s0 in the frozen beam), run on fresh generated 11-15-block problems.
proposals.why_now: Round 1 is the only lever with a registered system-level gain: P-11 direct 22 vs 8/110 (p=0.004), P-14 beam 88 vs 73/110 (+20/-5). But its direct gain stays inside the 6-10-block distillation range. H1 has 12 of its 13 successes in range, and on b3fresh v3 solves 7/74 at 11-15 (P-11, P-14 correction b). The remaining failure mass is at 11-15 (mirror B2: 44/74 failures vs 5/36). The F replay shows F is not binding, so the capability is in the proposer. The D-56/D-58 pipeline (bw_distill.py, bw_b3_prep.py, train_generic --init-adapter, bw_b3_eval.py) already exists. 25/110 Pa_v3 direct outputs hit M=256 (P-11), and longer 11-15 plans need a higher cap. Run it after item 7 (the release gate).
proposals.design:
Pre-registered addendum (PREREG_B6), written before any round-2 data exists.
- Search set: 160 fresh hard-style problems, 32 each at 11/12/13/14/15 blocks, seed 20261420 (BWM 202614xx; confirm unused). Generator: the b3fresh/mirror generator. Exclusions: hard signatures and invariants, val_large, mirror, b3fresh, seeds_fresh, distill-240, PB-600, val_v2, RCX E07/E07b/E08/E11a/E11b keys (research/b4_exclusions), and the B4 fresh set. Generate B4's set and B6's sets in one CPU step with mutual exclusion, without inspecting the B4 set. Disclose that the generator imitates hard's structure (H2 audit caveat a).
- Teacher: FREEZE_B3_H2 args with K=4 (the D-56 precedent; halves the cost) and E24. Keep only F-verified plans. The exact simulator is used for label precision only (analysis). Log the expansion at which each problem is solved (anytime curve, report-only).
- Rows: every suffix of each verified plan, with F-predicted states (D-56). Max-len 768; drops counted (D-58). Run a CPU token audit first.
- Arms (both start from Pa_v3; 400 steps, batch 16, lr 1e-4, seed 1):
  - Pa_v4 = round-2 rows plus an equal number of replay rows sampled from mix_v3, which carries the v2 and round-1 content as control-skill rows (X-04).
  - Pa_v3c = the same steps on replay rows only.
  - Recommended: a seed-2 copy of both arms.
- Primary: S-direct, greedy, M=512, on fresh b6fresh (n=110, hard block mix, seed 20261421). Pa_v4 vs Pa_v3c, exact McNemar. MET iff >= +10 pp and p < 0.05 (the B3 bar).
  - The M256 reading comes free: it is the 256-token prefix of the same greedy decode.
  - Key secondary: the 11-15 stratum (n=74).
  - Retention, report-only: val_v2-50 and the 6-10 stratum, with a -5 pp non-inferiority margin.
- C1, only if MET: S-beam on a fresh n=60 11-15 set (seed 20261422), FREEZE_B2_beam args, Pa_v4 vs Pa_v3c. This contrast is attribution-clean and closes H2 audit caveat 1. Run at E48 and read E24 as primary; E24 is identical by construction because sampling is per-candidate CRN and batch-independent (D-48c).
- C2, only if C1 is positive and the user approves the GPU time: a once-only hard run H2b = FREEZE_B2_beam with pa set to Pa_v4, 8 shards (D-50), paired vs H2.
- Report-only: illegal-proposal rate (F-cache replay), truncation, plan length relative to optimal, and teacher success per size.
- Byproducts at no extra GPU cost: a verified corpus for B4 arm b-sf (distance-to-go along F-verified plans) and for B5 macro mining.
proposals.expected_value:
Highest per turn. 3.5 turns cover search (~2), training of two adapters (~2.6 GPU-h) and the direct cells (~1 GPU-h). C1 adds ~2.5-3 turns and C2 ~2.
Round 1 gave +12.7 pp direct and +15/110 on the hard beam. Round 2 targets the stratum that holds most of the remaining failures. Plausible outcomes are direct 11-15 rising from ~7/74 to 15-25/74 and beam +4-8/60 at 11-15. It also produces about 3.5k F-verified rows that B4 and B5 reuse.
proposals.risks:
- Diminishing returns.
- A K4 teacher at 11-15 may verify few plans; K8 would double the search cost.
- Long, suboptimal teacher plans could raise truncation.
- The design is informed by hard's structure, which must be disclosed.
- Single seed unless the seed-2 copies are added.
- The beam gain may again fall off-stratum, as in H1/H2.
- GPU estimates are +/-50%.
- The B6 sets must be excluded from B4 and RCX draws.

proposals.title: B4 critic, amended for capability per turn: a futility screen first, no redundant arm, and a batched model-native value LoRA
proposals.question: Does a better child-ranking hook raise frozen-beam success? In RCX's GBFS with exact dynamics, the unmet key scores 0/75 at 200 expansions vs 39/75 for the hybrid (X-02, X-05). Can a Rineya-native value adapter supply the same signal?
proposals.why_now: The draft is ready (D-70, PREREG_B4_DRAFT.md), the exclusions are in hand (X-06), and RCX is waiting. As drafted, though, it means 5 beam arms at ~2 turns each on n=110. The F replay predicts that the invalid-state penalty almost never fires (c+pen ≈ c). Budget failures dominate: mirror B2 27 budget vs 22 dead end; H2 17 vs 5. A better key could convert some of these.
proposals.design:
Amendments for RCX to co-sign (BWM owns the final text; nothing is frozen yet):
1. Futility screen: a fresh dev set, n=40, 11-15 blocks, seed 20261411, B4 exclusions. Arms c+pen vs a under Pa_v2 at E24 (anytime-logged to E48). GO to the registered primary iff a solves >= 3 more than c+pen. Otherwise report 'not supported at screen' and leave the primary set unspent.
2. Drop arm c from the GPU plan. Report the hook counters to confirm c+pen ≈ c.
3. Arm b, a V-LoRA on Titan-Sparse:
   - h* labels from RCX's recipe (space.py sha 29d0b420, vendored), in BWM's seed range;
   - before the freeze, choose the target format on CPU-graded held-out goal classes: plain {"h": n} vs the X-04-style trace {"move": [blocks that must move], "h": n};
   - b-sf (distances from the B6 corpus) stays secondary;
   - batch V through an F wrapper that scores each newly predicted state in the same GPU call and caches by (state, goal), so the unmet= hook only reads the cache and the pinned planner is untouched.
4. Primary family unchanged: P1 a vs c+pen, P2 b vs c+pen, Holm, n=110, seed 20261410, E24. Secondary: E48 read from the same runs; mechanism metrics (actions advanced per expansion, budget vs dead-end share).
5. Pa_v3 cross as in D-70: c+pen and a under Pa_v3.
Label arms a and a0 tier B / hand-coded knowledge; only b counts as a Rineya capability.
proposals.expected_value:
The screen costs 1.5 turns. A GO adds about 7 (V-LoRA ~1, three primary arms ~6), and the Pa_v3 cross about 4 more.
Moderate to high under Pa_v2: plausibly +5-12/110 if the GBFS gap partly transfers. Smaller under Pa_v3 (at most 22 movable on hard). If b matches a, that is a model-native critic: a real capability gain for the small core, not an external module. A NO-GO saves about 7 turns.
proposals.risks:
- GBFS evidence may not transfer to a proposer-driven beam, and plateau length did not separate successes from failures.
- n=40 has low power; the bar is deliberately low and a NO-GO wording must avoid 'no effect'.
- V calls add GPU time.
- RCX's GNN is simulator-supervised, as is b-h*.
- Any change to the co-signed design needs RCX's agreement.

proposals.title: B-best: one combined frozen configuration, confirmed on a fresh set, then run once on Blocksworld-hard
proposals.question: How far do the separately tested gains (Pa round 2, critic hook, budget) add up in one system at a pre-stated compute budget? How does that system compare on hard with H2 (88/110), and (report-only, different regime) with the vendored per-instance R1 (59/110) and o1-preview (26/110) results?
proposals.why_now: Each lever is being tested alone against B2/H2 settings. Separate hard runs per lever would multiply hard-set exposures. One combined configuration chosen on generated data gives the honest headline for 'small world models rival larger models', and the anytime logs from B6/B4 provide most of the selection data for free.
proposals.expected_value:
About 5 turns: selection ~0.5-1 by reusing anytime logs, fresh 2 arms x 60 ~2.5, hard ~2.
If B6 and B4 each convert a few failures, hard could reach roughly 92-100/110, a wider gap over R1's 59/110 (still a different regime). It also yields a success-vs-compute curve: the strongest pre-registered, honest capability statement available.
proposals.risks:
- Forking paths if the grid grows; keep it small and fixed in advance.
- Ceiling effect (22 movable on hard).
- E48 raises compute, so compute must be reported alongside success.
- Hard is used again (B2, H1/H2, B-best). Mitigations: fresh confirmation first, no setting chosen on hard, one run.
- The published comparators are 2024-25 models.

proposals.title: Move legality-trace supervision to item 9 Logistics, where the delta parser cannot catch false 'legal' answers
proposals.question: Does a Logistics F trained with the D-52 cmp/calc/after trace keep false-legal near zero on illegal actions whose violated precondition is never deleted (vehicle at the location, in-city, airport, types)? Does that protect the verification precision of imagined plans?
proposals.why_now: Finding (2) shows Blocksworld's support check made FK's legality loss harmless. bench/planbench/logistics/generated_domain.pddl never deletes at ?truck ?loc, at ?airplane ?loc, in-city, AIRPORT or the type facts. So the ~24% of illegal proposals that the Blocksworld F caught only through the parser would pass as legal in Logistics, giving verified-but-invalid plans. RCWM's LB showed this failure class: T2's verified-plan precision was 0.952 (D-61). X-04 shows traces teach computed predicates (0.90 vs 0.39 plain). The item 9 prereg is still a draft (D-67, D-69), so the arm can be added before the freeze, and LMForwardD already takes an F max_new parameter (domain_planner.py), so the pinned planner is untouched.
proposals.design:
Add to PREREG_LOGISTICS before its freeze:
(i) An 'undeletable-precondition' stratum in lg_forward_grade.py (seed 20261404). Promote it from report-only to a pre-test gate: F must show false-legal <= 2% on the stratum and verification precision >= 0.98 on LG-VAL-OUT, or the PlanBench test is not run (the futility-gate pattern).
(ii) A second F arm, LG_FT: the same 12k keys plus control rows (X-04 rule). Target in the D-52 schema: cmp lists each precondition fact with its truth, calc = the delta, after = the answer. Raise F max_new via LMForwardD. The constant-length filler control (D-55) is optional.
(iii) A pre-stated selection rule between LG_F and LG_FT on generated keys only (false-legal on the stratum first, then exact match), applied before any planner run. Report RCWM's false-copy metric (X-01).
The Blocksworld trace-F is deferred.
proposals.expected_value:
About 1 extra turn inside item 9 (FT training ~2 GPU-h with longer targets; key grading on the CPU lane).
High protective value for a ~6-turn programme. It turns a likely silent failure into a measured, gated quantity, and it extends the cross-programme 'computed predicate' finding to a second planning domain.
proposals.risks:
- Trace outputs make each F query more expensive.
- RCWM 5a's joint trace induced copying (false copy 0.29; X-01), so false copy must be measured.
- One seed.
- Adds a decision point to a draft the user must confirm.

proposals.title: Use D-54: test FK inside the frozen planner on a held-out key order (the PREREG-4 mirror committed in D-63)
proposals.question: Does the key-order-augmented F plan as well in a held-out serialization as F0 does in the canonical one, turning F-08's 'format-locked' caveat into a tested planning-level claim for F?
proposals.why_now: D-63 commits BWM to this mirror. Finding (2) shows FK's planning-effective accuracy is 0.996 on both held-out orders, vs 0.454-0.496 for F0, so a pass is likely and cheap. It also lines up with RCWM's T2b-ledger/PREREG-4 and RCX's surface-diversity result (X-06).
proposals.expected_value:
0.5 turn for Stage 1, plus 1.5 if Stage 2 runs.
Moderate capability value (robustness of the world model in planning) and high honesty value. It retires part of a standing caveat at low cost.
proposals.risks:
- Pa is still format-locked.
- heldout_both (renamed + reordered + shuffled) is only 0.942 effective.
- One FK seed.
- FK's canonical exact accuracy is 0.963 even though its planner-effective accuracy is 1.000; this must be explained.

proposals.title: Blocksworld-XL: a size curriculum beyond PlanBench (16-25 blocks), starting on CPU
proposals.question: How far does learned F + search extrapolate past every size it has seen? F was trained on <= 6 blocks; Pa was distilled on <= 10 blocks (<= 15 after B6). Do the proposer and F handle object names beyond a..o?
proposals.why_now: F-05/F-07 show F exact to 15 blocks (delta 1.000), and the replay shows F essentially error-free in planning, so the size frontier is set by Pa and budget. B.NAMES has only 15 names (a..o), so more than 15 blocks also tests name generalization (F-08: F 0.992 on unseen names; Pa untested). This sets the target range for a later round.
proposals.design:
- CPU lane (0 GPU): grade F0 and FK at 16/18/20/25 blocks with names beyond a..o, 60 keys per size, half illegal, scored both exact and planner-effective (F-05 method). Also a Pa prompt-length audit at 20-25 blocks.
- GPU, report-only stress test: XL-40 fresh set (10 each at 16/18/20/22 blocks; seed 20261430) with the H2 configuration (later B-best) at E48 anytime. max_depth stays 80, which can bind near 22 blocks; report it.
- Pre-stated outputs: success by size, failure mode, and F errors via replay.
- If Pa collapses on new names or sizes, the next distillation round adds a 16-18-block slice with an extended name pool.
proposals.expected_value: About 1.25 turns. Medium. It is the cleanest out-of-size extrapolation evidence (beyond the benchmark's range), it locates the frontier for round 3, and no published comparator is needed.
proposals.risks:
- Pa may score ~0 because of unseen names or sizes.
- Long prompts and states make each instance expensive.
- max_depth 80 may bind.
- Descriptive only.

proposals.title: B5 macros: harness pre-screen first, GPU only on a clear signal
proposals.question: Do RCX's mined macros (E11a: 52 -> 77/120 at 200 expansions in GBFS) help a proposer-driven beam, where Pa already emits multi-action plans?
proposals.why_now: The inputs are vendored and verified (X-07 follow-up: libraries.json b61b4a05). But E11a's gain was in primitive-action GBFS. With beam4 the random library collapsed (23/120), and with misplaced_blocks any library helped about equally (R-09). Library M is mostly tower-building chains, which Pa already writes. Expected value inside plan_beam is therefore uncertain and should be screened cheaply.
proposals.design:
Stage 0 (CPU, 0 GPU): run the pinned plan_beam through the stub-import harness, with ExactF and scripted proposers on fresh generated 11-15-block instances.
- Macros enter as extra zero-token candidates, with goal-gated bindings instantiated only when consistent with the imagined state (X-07 notes).
- Arms P/M/R/S at E12 and E24, compute-matched by F queries.
- GO iff M - max(R, S) >= +5/120 and M - P >= +5 at E24.
Stage 1, only on GO: a prereg co-signed with RCX. Arms P vs M, with S as the attribution control, Pa_v3 in the frozen beam, fresh n=60 11-15 set. Primary M vs P; attribution M vs S.
proposals.expected_value:
0 GPU turns for the harness; about 3 more if Stage 1 runs.
Low to moderate. The most plausible benefit is fewer proposer tokens per solve, an efficiency gain rather than more solves.
proposals.risks:
- The harness proposers are not Pa.
- Macro candidates may crowd out Pa's candidates.
- Needs a new candidate-injection module.
- RCX's specificity ('mined beats shuffled') depended on the heuristic.

props.lens: EXTERNAL VALIDITY: the question is whether small Rineya world models really rival larger models on real tasks. Every external number so far is either a different-regime, unpaired published reference (R1 53.6%, o1-preview 23.6%), with compute that is unknown or uncounted, or a single-domain, single-seed internal contrast (P-10, P-14). Four things are missing: (a) a compute ledger, which E-01(c) lists as never run; (b) the same-harness local comparators that PREREG_PLANBENCH registered but never ran, now feasible because Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B are already in the local HF cache; (c) a second domain (item 9); (d) a benchmark that tests the world model itself (PlanBench Task 7) rather than only planning success. Suggested order: start #1 now on CPU. Run #2 and #4 on the BWM CPU lane during RCWM's GPU turns, alongside item 7. On the GPU, run item 7, then item 9 (#3), ahead of B4/B5: their headline arms are tier-B external-module results that add no external validity (PREREG_B4 §1; X-07). After that, #5/#6, then the #7 screen. Rough estimate from my scratch calculation with bwmn/flops.py, to be made exact in #1: H2 costs about 0.9e14 inference FLOPs per instance, of which 198 F queries × ~3.2e11 is the bulk. R1 costs roughly 6e14 (37B active × ~8.4k tokens, from the upstream usage fields), about 7× more. Iso-FLOP budgets: about 10.8k tokens for Qwen3-4B and about 5.7k for Qwen3-8B.

proposals.title: Compute and comparability ledger, plus vendoring and VAL re-scoring of published per-instance files (prerequisite)
proposals.question: For each frozen BWM result (B2 hard/mirror/600, H1, H2), what are the inference FLOPs per instance? How do they compare with the measured token usage of published systems? And what are the paired, local-VAL-scored comparisons on identical instance IDs?
proposals.why_now: E-01(c) records 'not run: FLOPs/F-token accounting', a registered B2 secondary in PREREG_PLANBENCH.md. P-14(d) and research/H2_LEAK_CLAIMS_AUDIT.json say the upstream per-instance hard results (R1 59/110, o1-preview 26/110, o1-mini 1/110 at step 0) and the post hoc pairing (H2 vs R1 +36/-7, p = 9e-6; B2 vs R1 +30/-16, p = 0.054) cannot be cited until vendored with sha256 and re-scored by the local VAL. Those files sit only in Temp scratch (C:/Users/clclc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bwm_h2_scratch/dl_upstream_hard). They carry API usage fields; my read gives median completion tokens of R1 7,814, o1-preview 7,805 and o1-mini 12,396 on hard. Any iso-FLOP comparator (#2, #3, #4) needs its budget fixed from this ledger before it runs.
proposals.design: CPU only; registered as a report-only accounting addendum. (a) Vendor (user approval needed, D-67 precedent) the upstream fc638a1a files into bench/planbench/results/ with sha256 recorded in SOURCE.md: hard per-instance results for R1, o1-preview and o1-mini; Task-7 prompts and results; randomized-obfuscated Blocksworld results. Re-score every plan with the local VAL (planbench_ledger.py pattern). (b) BWM FLOPs per instance from existing artifacts only: per-shard fcache.jsonl for unique F keys actually computed (the FR-02 cache-hit lesson), plans.jsonl gen_tokens/rounds, and prompt lengths rebuilt by re-rendering through blocks.render_chat with the tokenizer only (no torch). Count with bwmn/flops.py using the shared-prefix formula for the K samples. Report dense, attention and LM-head terms for B2, H1, H2 and S-direct on hard, mirror and 600, plus wall time. (c) Published compute: R1 FLOPs estimated from its public config × usage tokens and labelled 'estimated'; o1 tokens reported, FLOPs 'unknown' (PREREG_PLANBENCH comparability ledger). (d) Post hoc paired exact McNemar against each re-scored published file on identical IDs, Holm across files, labelled post hoc. (e) A comparability table with one row per comparator and columns: training regime, input (PDDL text vs code-parsed JSON), feedback, compute (measured/estimated/unknown), pairing, scorer, seeds. Claim templates taken verbatim from the audit's 'headline'; banned wordings listed (no 'beats o1/R1', no 'simulator-free', no 'trained only on <= 6 blocks' for Pa_v3, o1-mini only as 0.9% direct). (f) Compute and freeze the iso-FLOP token budgets for #2, #3 and #4 from H2's measured mean.
proposals.expected_value: It closes the only unrun registered B2 secondary. It turns the strongest rivalry evidence (H2 vs R1, paired) into a citable, VAL-scored post hoc statement. It gives the first compute-normalized sentence, e.g. 'about 1/7 of R1's estimated per-instance inference FLOPs', with the right labels. It fixes the comparator budgets before any comparator output exists, so they cannot be tuned. Everything else in this list depends on it.
proposals.risks: R1 FLOP estimates ignore MoE routing and API-side overheads, so they must say 'estimated'. o1 compute stays unknown. Prompt-token reconstruction must match the exact render path, or the BWM FLOPs drift (validate on a few instances by replaying the token counts). The paired published comparisons stay post hoc. The vendoring write needs the user's approval.

proposals.title: Same-harness Qwen3-4B (thinking at an iso-FLOP budget, and non-thinking) on Blocksworld-hard, paired with H2/B2
proposals.question: On identical Blocksworld-hard instances, with the same local VAL, the same machine and matched inference FLOPs, does the frozen 0.6B Rineya with LoRA world model and beam search (H2 88/110; B2 73/110) solve more than an open 4B reasoning model? How much does Qwen gain from a larger thinking budget?
proposals.why_now: PREREG_PLANBENCH.md (Comparators 1) registered same-harness Qwen3 arms, with allowed headline (b) 'iso-FLOP non-inferiority vs Qwen3-4B-thinking'. They were never run (D-27 Track C; research/SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md §2 'still pending'). scripts/planbench_qwen.py (875 lines) exists. TODO_BEFORE_RUNS.md still shows 9 unchecked must-fix items, although the script docstring and bwmn/planbench_extract.py suggest most are done. Qwen3-4B (7.6 GB) and Qwen3-8B (16 GB) snapshots are complete in the local HF cache, and the machine has 31 GB RAM. Every current external comparison is 'different regime, unknown compute'. This is the only fully comparable 'larger model' data point, and it needs no GPU.
proposals.design:
PREREG_LOCAL_COMPARATORS.md, frozen before any Qwen output on any listed set.

Systems:
- Q4T-iso: Qwen3-4B thinking with Qwen sampling (T 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, fixed per-instance seed). Its total token budget equals H2's mean FLOPs per instance from #1 (about 10.8k tokens including the prompt), enforced by budget forcing as in planbench_qwen.py.
- Q4T-iso/4: a descriptive point on the budget curve.
- Q4N: non-thinking, greedy, max-new 1024.
- Optional, descriptive: Qwen3-8B at its iso budget (about 5.7k tokens) on 20 instances, only when at least 20 GB RAM is free and every other lane is idle.

Prompt: exactly the zero-shot PDDL prompt R1 and o1 saw, taken from the vendored upstream hard files and sha-pinned, with PlanBench's system message.

Instances:
- Q4T: a 40-instance hard subset stratified by sorted block count (every 110/40-th; IDs and sha listed in the prereg).
- Q4N: all 110.
- Throughput is measured on 3 PB-600 instances before n is fixed. n never changes after the first hard output.

Scoring: local VAL with the primary extractor plus PlanBench's text_to_plan as a second scorer; disagreements are reported.

Primary test: H2 (frozen, already run once; its per-instance results on the 40 are fixed) vs Q4T-iso, exact McNemar.
- 'Rineya system higher at matched compute' iff b > c and p < 0.05.
- 'Non-inferior' iff the Newcombe paired 95% lower bound > -0.05.
- Otherwise 'not shown'.

Report-only:
- B2 vs Q4T;
- Q4N vs B2/H2 on all 110;
- Q4T vs the R1/o1-preview per-instance files (post hoc);
- results by block count;
- FLOPs and wall time;
- the budget-forced truncation rate.

Contamination control: Q4N, and Q4T if CPU time allows, on item 7's seeds_fresh-40 with the same PDDL template rendered from the generated instances, paired against R0/R1/R2 S-beam (this also gives a seed spread). A gap above 10 pp is flagged.

Gates: exclusive lock, at least 12 GB RAM, no other native_v1 job (so it runs during RCWM turns), D-35 CPU patch, pinned resume config, RCX CPU lane and RAM floors respected (D-64).
proposals.expected_value: The first in-harness, compute-measured 'small vs larger model' result. Given o1-preview's 23.6% zero-shot, the likely outcome supports: 'at matched inference FLOPs, on identical PlanBench Blocksworld-hard instances and the same validator, a 0.6B Rineya world model + search solves X/40 vs Qwen3-4B-thinking Y/40'. That sentence still needs the 'domain-trained specialist vs zero-shot generalist' caveat. If Qwen comes close, the redirect is equally valuable. The budget curve shows whether more thinking would close the gap.
proposals.risks: CPU throughput is unknown; at an assumed 3-6 tok/s, Q4T on 40 instances is about 25-45 CPU-h, and Q4N on 110 about 3-5 CPU-h. The 'no other native_v1 job' gate limits it to about 50% duty, so it may take 3-5 days. Qwen pretraining may include PlanBench hard. That inflates Qwen and is conservative for BWM claims, which is why the fresh-40 control matters. Budget forcing can truncate Qwen; report the curve, not only the iso point. The training regime still differs (#5 addresses same-data). With n = 40, only large differences are detectable.

proposals.title: Item 9 Logistics transfer, with external-validity amendments before the freeze, moved ahead of B4/B5
proposals.question: In a second PlanBench domain, does a learned F plus imagined search beat the same proposer alone out of size range (1-3 packages in training, 4-7 at test)? Where does that place a 0.6B system relative to same-harness and published larger models on identical Logistics instances?
proposals.why_now: The user chose Logistics as the strongest generality claim (D-65.5). CPU-1 and CPU-2 are done (D-69): logistics.py passes 33/33 tests, the A* teacher is optimal on 285/285, and the published re-score covers 1,450 plans with 0 disagreements. CPU-3 to CPU-5 remain. The current queue puts item 9 after item 7, B4 and B5. B4's arm (a) and B5 are tier-B external-module results: PREREG_B4_DRAFT §1 says (a) does not establish LM-planner improvement, and X-07 says 'nothing is internalized in Rineya'. They raise Blocksworld numbers without adding external validity. Every current claim is one domain and one seed (P-10, P-14).
proposals.design:
Keep research/PREREG_LOGISTICS_DRAFT.md:
- train on 1-3 packages; select C1-C3 on LG-VAL-IN/OUT;
- futility gate: GO iff S-beam >= 4/20 and >= +3 over S-direct on LG-VAL-OUT;
- P1: S-beam vs S-direct on PB-OUT-80, YES iff >= +0.20 and p < 0.01;
- MIRROR-80 contamination flag; Stage C conditional.

Add before the freeze:
- (A1) A same-harness Qwen3-4B arm on PB-OUT-80, report-only and paired: Q4N on all 80, and Q4T at an iso-FLOP budget from the selected S-beam's measured selection-set cost, on the 63 IDs that o1-preview's file covers. Prompt: o1-preview's zero-shot PDDL prompt text from the vendored result file.
- (A2) Exact FLOP accounting for S-beam and S-direct, registered using #1's code.
- (A3) Logistics Task 7: the 285 PlanBench prompts with LG_F chained, report-only. This measures the world model independently of planning, and is informative even on a NO-GO.
- (A4) A conditional Stage D, registered now (B3 analogue): self-distill LG_Pa on F-verified plans of generated 4-5-package problems, with exclusions and its own fresh set, run only if P1 = YES/PARTIAL and the user approves.
- (A5) Claim wording: o1-preview's 59/63 on the covered IDs is expected to be higher. 'Rival' language is allowed only against the same-harness Qwen arm at matched FLOPs. Literature on SFT size collapse is quoted as context only, still marked [VERIFY].

Queue: item 7 → item 9 (bundleL1 onward) → B4 → B5.
proposals.expected_value: Either a second-domain replication of the world-model effect, which licenses 'the recipe's world-model-plus-search effect holds out of size range in two PlanBench domains (one seed each)', or an honest negative through the futility gate, with no PlanBench instance spent. The Qwen arm places the 0.6B system against a larger open model in a domain where o1-preview is strong (94%), which keeps the rivalry framing honest.
proposals.risks: Logistics has plateaus: `unmet` drops only when a package is delivered. The default ranking key is weak (RCX R-04: unmet-goal policy accuracy 0.06), so a NO-GO is plausible; the draft's R-window grid is the only mitigation. Max-len 768 raises VRAM and time, to be re-measured in the bundleL1 smoke test. 63 of the 80 PB-OUT-80 IDs have published o1 coverage. Single seed. About 16-38 GPU-h (D-67), which delays B4/B5 by about 2-3 days.

proposals.title: PlanBench Task 7 (plan execution) as a world-model benchmark, plus a registered long-horizon fresh variant (Task 7-L)
proposals.question: As a consequence predictor, how does the frozen BW_Fdelta_s0, chained step by step, compare with larger LMs on PlanBench's own plan-execution task? Does its advantage grow with horizon and block count, where in-context state tracking degrades?
proposals.why_now: The programme's central object is a world model, but every external number is planning success. F's accuracy has only been measured on generated keys (F-05, F-07, F-08, P-12). PlanBench Task 7 prompts exist in the upstream clone (…/scratchpad/LLMs-Planning/plan-bench/prompts/{blocksworld,blocksworld_3,logistics,mystery_blocksworld}/task_7_plan_execution.json: 500/100/285/500), with published per-instance GPT-4 results: 142/500 and 49/100, and text-davinci-002 3/500 and 1/100 (upstream llm_correct flags, not re-scored). No GPU is needed.
proposals.design:
PREREG_TASK7.md.

(i) F-chain: code parses the instance PDDL and the prompt's NL action sequence, using PlanBench's own NL↔PDDL mapping, unit-tested against ground_truth_plan. It renders states in the canonical training format (F-08 format lock), applies F's delta k times (greedy, no search, no simulator) and maps the final facts to PlanBench's fact list.
(ii) Same-harness Qwen3-4B: non-thinking on all 600, and thinking at a fixed budget on a stratified 100.
(iii) Published GPT-4 and davinci per-instance files, vendored and re-graded.

Metric: exact final-state match under PlanBench's grader. Secondary: per-fact F1 and agreement with the exact simulator.

Task 7-L (fresh, registered):
- 110 generated instances of 6-15 blocks (seed 202614xx; item-7 exclusions plus research/b4_exclusions lists);
- action sequences of 10-40 steps (prefixes of A* plans and random legal walks);
- in half the items, one illegal action whose correct handling is 'state unchanged' (this tests the legality predicate that P-12 found fragile).

Primary on 7-L: F-chain vs Qwen3-4B-thinking, paired exact McNemar. 'World model more accurate' iff b > c and p < 0.05. Qwen gets at least the iso-FLOP budget, and the report states that the F-chain uses about k × 3.2e11 FLOPs, i.e. less compute.

Report: accuracy vs horizon k and vs block count.
proposals.expected_value: A public-benchmark world-model result ('a 0.6B learned world model predicts plan-execution outcomes at X% vs GPT-4 28.4% (paired) and Qwen3-4B Y%'), plus a horizon curve showing where an explicit learned simulator beats in-context state tracking. That is the mechanism behind every planning result. The same harness serves Logistics (A3 in #3) and the Mystery screen (#7). Cheap: about 5-6k F calls (about 3 CPU-h) and about 10-20 CPU-h for Qwen.
proposals.risks: PB Task 7 (3-5 blocks, short sequences) is near ceiling for F (F-05: exact on all generated keys at 3-10 blocks, 1.000 for the state format), and its published comparator is a 2023 one-shot GPT-4. 'Beats GPT-4' is not news (PREREG_PLANBENCH ledger); the information is in 7-L and the Qwen pairing. A bug in the NL action parser would look like an F error, so audit it against ground truth first. The rendering must use the canonical key order. Vendoring the Task 7 assets needs the user's approval.

proposals.title: Same-data larger-model SFT comparator: Qwen3-1.7B LoRA proposer, planning directly (does scale substitute for the world model?)
proposals.question: Trained on exactly the same <= 6-block proposer rows, does a ~3x larger LM planning directly, with no world model, approach the 0.6B system with world model and search out of size range?
proposals.why_now: The SFT-collapse evidence (SOLUTIONS §1.5: a Gemma2-9B LoRA trained on 3-5 blocks falls to 53% at 6 blocks and 0% at 10) comes from other harnesses. Reviewers will ask of P-10/P-14: 'would a bigger model trained on your data just solve it?' Only 0.6B S-direct exists in this harness (B2 5/110; Pa_v3 13/110). #2 covers larger zero-shot models but not same-data training.
proposals.expected_value: In-harness evidence that the world model plus search, not parameter count, carries out-of-range planning: the core of 'small world models rival larger models'. If Q17 S-direct matches B2 S-beam, that falsifies the narrative cheaply and early.
proposals.risks: Qwen3-1.7B is not in the local HF cache, so a download (network plus approval) is needed. BF16 vs FP32 is a confound, declared. 3x is a modest scale step; a 4B or 8B SFT does not fit the 8 GB laptop GPU without quantization. blocks_eval.py hard-codes titan-sparse (line 107) and train_generic needs BF16 support, so additive --core options are needed. It uses about 2 GPU turns that compete with item 7 and item 9.

proposals.title: Rineya attribution screen: stock Qwen3-0.6B vs Titan-Sparse under the identical F recipe (staged)
proposals.question: Does the Rineya core earn the 'Rineya' in the claims, or does stock Qwen3-0.6B (same architecture; Titan descends from Supa-1.7.0) with the same LoRA recipe give an equally good world model?
proposals.why_now: Every allowed claim says 'a frozen 0.6B Rineya'. RCWM X-01 and R10 show Titan's one-step prior differs before adaptation, but no BWM experiment isolates the core after 12k-transition LoRA training. Item 7 is training F seeds now (runs/BW_Fdelta_s1/log.txt at step 400/600), which supplies a Titan seed spread as the yardstick. qwen3-0.6b is already in lm.MODELS (FP32).
proposals.design:
Stage 1 (registered screen): train Q06_F on Qwen3-0.6B with the exact BW_Fdelta_s0 recipe (forward_delta_train.jsonl, 600 steps, seed 0, FP32, max-len 256).

CPU grading on fresh generated keys (seed 202614xx, item-7 exclusions):
- exact match by block count, 3-15 blocks, 60 keys each, about 50% illegal;
- the F-08/P-12 surface modes (canonical, reversed key order, unseen names).

Compared with BW_Fdelta_s0 and item 7's F seeds 1 and 2. Reading:
- 'core matters for F' iff, pooled over 11-15 blocks, Q06_F lies outside the [min, max] of the three Titan seeds by more than 2 pp with paired McNemar p < 0.01 against the nearest seed;
- otherwise 'no core effect detected'.

Stage 2 (conditional on 'core matters', separate approval): a Q06 Pa and the full system on seeds_fresh-40 as an item-7-style system RQ.
proposals.expected_value: It decides whether the model card can attribute the world model to Rineya or must say 'a 0.6B LM with LoRA'. Both answers are publishable and needed for honest claims. Stage 1 is about 1.65 GPU-h plus CPU grading, and can ride the tail of a BWM turn.
proposals.risks: If both F models are at ceiling, the screen cannot discriminate; the illegal and held-out-order strata are the hardest available. proposals.title: Gated rule-reading screen for Mystery and randomized-obfuscated Blocksworld (Regime B) before any planning claim
proposals.question: Can a LoRA world model on frozen Titan-Sparse execute the actions of an unseen domain whose rules are given in the prompt? If so, PlanBench Mystery and randomized-obfuscated Blocksworld become genuine transfer tests rather than renamings handled by code.
proposals.design:
Stage S (prereg, screen only):
- Close the TODO items: suffix-signature guard, vocabulary filter, single-letter objects, Blocksworld-fragment exclusion, token budget, signature-clustered CIs (603 Mystery instances = 262 problems).
- Generate Regime B data: random lifted STRIPS domains with the fixed rule template `name(X,Y): pre[..] add[..] del[..]`.
- Train two F arms (seed 0, D-03): plain delta, and the D-52 cmp/calc/after trace (X-04). Both include control rows (X-04 lesson); report a false-apply metric (X-01).
- Evaluate one-step and Task-7-style execution on held-out generated domains and on PlanBench Mystery Task 7 (500). Rules are converted from the PDDL domain by code (format conversion only, no semantic mapping).

Gate: a new prereg for planning (Pa_B plus beam on Mystery Task 1) only if the best arm reaches Mystery Task-7 exact >= 0.80 and illegal-action no-op accuracy >= 0.90.
proposals.expected_value: A pass opens the only route to a 'reasons from rules given in the prompt' claim, on the axis where 400B-600B+ models are far from ceiling, which would be the strongest form of 'rivals larger models'. The more likely fail, given R-03/R-05/X-06, is a clean, cheap negative that bounds the claims ('domain-trained; does not read new rules') and saves the 4+ turns a planning attempt would cost.
proposals.risks: High prior of failure. Long rule prompts raise memory and time. Evaluating on PlanBench Mystery Task 7 spends those instances for this F. Results must be clustered by signature. It competes with item 9 for GPU, so run it only after #3's futility gate is known.
